plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A graceful ornamental tree that covers its bare branches in clouds of delicate, five-petaled blossoms before the leaves emerge. It is the most widely planted cherry in Japan and in many temperate cities worldwide.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April in temperate Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. (USA), Korea, and temperate parks and gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: The Yoshino cherry trees around the Tidal Basin in Washington D.C. were a gift from Tokyo in 1912, and their peak bloom is celebrated each spring with the National Cherry Blossom Festival.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A hardy bulbous perennial with nodding yellow trumpet-shaped flowers surrounded by paler yellow petals. It grows in woodlands and meadows and is the ancestor of many garden daffodil cultivars.
plants.location: Western Europe, especially the UK, France, and Belgium; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: All parts of the daffodil contain lycorine and other alkaloids, which make it toxic to most grazing animals, and one of its compounds, galantamine, is used in medicine to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: A small deciduous tree with heart-shaped leaves whose magenta-pink flowers burst directly from the branches and even the trunk before the foliage appears. It is a favorite of early-season pollinators.
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from Ontario to Mexico
plants.funFact: Redbud blooms are edible and are sometimes tossed into salads or fried, and the flowers are cauliflorous, meaning they grow directly out of old wood.

plants.name: Amaryllis belladonna
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up bare, sturdy stalks topped with clusters of fragrant, trumpet-shaped pink flowers. The strap-like leaves appear after flowering. It thrives in Mediterranean-type climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: March to April in the Southern Hemisphere (autumn)
plants.location: Western Cape of South Africa; naturalized in Australia, New Zealand, and California
plants.funFact: Because the flower stalks emerge without any leaves in autumn, the plant is often called the 'naked lady' in Australia and California.
